utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-84-T, the Prosecutor versus Ramush Haradinaj et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Is the Defence ready to continue the cross-examination of Mr. Crosland?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. May I indicate that Your Honours should have before you an amended version of the index to binder 1, which contains those exhibits which have so far been marked for identification with either a P or a D number. What I propose to do, subject to any expression of view from the Trial Chamber, is to continue the cross-examination in the same format as before; in other words, to cross-examine the witness by reference to tab number only because that is the way that the first half of the cross-examination was conducted; but then at the end of his evidence to have each of the other documents marked for identification and this index will then be updated and the further version provided to the Trial Chamber. So what this is in effect a work in progress so Your Honours know what we're looking at any point in time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of that. At the same time, if it would ever come to a situation where others would have to review the transcripts of these hearings, then it might be good that they do not find tab numbers and MFI numbers separated. Therefore, if you refer to any document that has already received an MFI number, you're invited to --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- mention that immediately; and if not, to have them linked as quickly as possible so I'll then invite Madam Registrar to assign a D MFI number immediately so that we find that on the record concentrated in one spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I have no difficulty at all with that, simply to observe that for whatever reason that's not the way I dealt with the first half of the cross-examination so there will be a disconcurrence on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think as a matter of fact let's continue with the system which has some flaws but would be a better idea and, therefore, rather to improve than to stick to the old system. Then Madam Usher, would you please escort Mr. Crosland into the courtroom. May I take it that the parties would agree that reminding Mr. Crosland that he is still bound by the solemn declaration, although given some time ago, would at this moment do rather than to invite him to make that solemn declaration again.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Absolutely. As far as timing is concerned, I've had an opportunity to discuss this issue with Mr. Guy-Smith. May we simply give Your Honours the collective assurance that our cross-examinations taken together will conclude today, with Mr. Harvey cross-examining first thing in the morning for a relatively a brief period when he returns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and then we could continue with the next witness tomorrow after Mr. Harvey is cross-examine is completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The only issue, of course, is that if you would finish earlier today, then we might have to wait for Mr. Harvey before re-examination would start, which is, of course, not a preferred situation. Mr. Re, you understand that I would rather not invite you to start any re-examination before we have heard the cross-examination -- the testimony and cross-examination by Mr. Harvey.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I wouldn't be in a position to re-examine before Mr. Harvey in reality, because he may cross over material which I would have no re-re-examine on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. The Chamber is concerned about any loss of time, and since we have still other witnesses for the remainder of the week --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think, if I may say so, it is unlikely that we will finish very substantially before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- the end of the day. I may prove to be wrong on that, but I think it's unlikely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Crosland.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Crosland, on the 19th of April, you gave your solemn declaration that you would speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. That solemn declaration still binds you in the testimony you are about to give. The expectation is that it will take today and a part of tomorrow's hearing for your testimony. Mr. Emmerson will now continue to cross-examine you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Good morning, Colonel Crosland. We're all grateful to you for making the time to come back.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I remind you of something I was reminded of myself this morning, which the need for us both to speak slowly and leave a clear pause between question and answer, both for translation and for transcription purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could the witness please be provided with the green and the blue binders.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think, as before, Colonel Crosland, you can for the time being put the blue binder to the one side and concentrate, if you will, with me on the green binder. And I had embarked at the end of the last occasion when you were here on going through a number of documents with you chronologically to look at Serbian troop deployments and military engagements in the area with which this indictment is concerned. We had reached tab 14 in the binder when we adjourned, and you will remember there was some discussion in response to an observation from Judge Orie about the implications of the word "axis" in a particular document. I'll allow you in just a moment to refresh your memory. So behind tab 14, we find a 16th of May order regarding the redeployment of the 125th Motorised Brigade, which is based in Peje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In line with what I said earlier, we'll invite Madam Registrar to assign a number to tab 14.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D70.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it is, as I say, a memorandum signed by Colonel Zivanovic, regarding a deployment of the 125th Brigade, which was then, I think, you've confirmed, based in Pec. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understand, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So if we turn to page 2, which is where we had concentrated our attention on the last occasion, it refers in the first two paragraphs to the proposed deployment of BG-2, that is combat group 2, and BG-3, that is combat group 3, of the 125th. Pausing for a moment - and we discussed this briefly on the last occasion, but just to re-orientate ourselves - the 125th was based in Pec and the 549th under Colonel Delic was based in Prizren. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was correct at the time, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So looking again at the first entry, combat group 2, and bearing in mind Judge Orie's observations on the language, one can see, if I just read it briefly into the record, that "combat group 2 is instructed to be at the ready in the current redeployment sector for operations along the following axes," and then two axes are set out. The first is an axis beginning at the barracks; and assuming that the barracks were in the location of the deployment of the 125th, that would presumably mean Pec. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what it appears to mean, Mr. Emmerson, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So from the barracks to Smonica and from Smonica to Ponosevac and from Ponosevac to Gornja Morina, all of which would be on the west side of the road; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That appears to be correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So on the face of it, whether this order was carried into effect or not, this is an order for combat group 2 to be deployed in a manoeuvre moving southwards from Pec as far as Gornja Morina?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then the second axis there referred to is from the barracks, again, to Erecka Suka, and immediately after that what appears to be a third axis of deployment from the barracks to Zrze and the barracks to Radonjic Lake. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So on the face of it, this is a series of radiating deployments, beginning at Pec, heading southwards on both sides of the main road. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That appears to be what they'd been ordered to do so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: With a target or a series of targets which include both Erecka Suka and Radonjic Lake?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the task is there described in language which, would you agree, suggests that they are going to be meeting and cooperating with MUP forces deployed in those areas, because it reads tasks: "In cooperated action with neighbouring forces of the Republic of Serbia MUP break up Siptar sabotage and terrorist groups and secure supply routes for VJ units."

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if carried into effect, that would be a fairly comprehensive sweep downwards by the 125th to clear both sides of the main road. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That, on the surface, appears, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Moving down towards the area which was under the responsibility of the 549th?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, before you continue, I noticed that you're talking about a memo; whereas, in the draft translation we find under tab 14, it is said it is an order; and I then was informed by Madam Registrar that the uploaded document, so I take it that it's 65 ter 424, is only in the original language and that no translation or even a draft translation has been attached. Since I would like to know for certain that we are talking about documents, the documents we find in our binder, are the same as the ones in the electronic court system, I wonder what to do. It's also difficult, I take it, for Madam Registrar -- I don't know whether it -- the original is now assigned the D70 number. Yes. Perhaps you could have a look at that -- yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The case manager, Mr. Smith, has located a translation that we have. I hope that it has been disclosed to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I would like to know, if it's not uploaded in the system, there always is a risk of having several translations of the same document, and I just want to verify that we are all talking about the same original and about the same translation. If you could please work on that, I would not --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I do not attempt to stop you at this moment, but at least this will be settled soon.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Your Honour will appreciate the way in which these translations come into our possession. We requested the Prosecution to provide us with English translations of the documents that had been supplied by a number of Serbian military officials, including Colonel Delic, and we were supplied with draft translations. I am not aware of having been supplied with a final translation of this document. Had there been one, we would have put it into the system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We can certainly clarify the position and ensure that the accurate translation is the one that is linked to the original document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'll resolve that with that and any other document in which the situation arises during the course of today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But in so far as the word "memo" is concerned, that is my mistake because this translation clearly uses the order "order."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just coming back, if I may, to the implications of that. Were you, yourself, aware, Colonel Crosland, of a deployment of Serb forces southwards from Pec, let us say, at any point in the second half of May?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, no, we were obviously not aware. We would not be told anything that the VJ or the MUP would be doing. My observations were as we saw and identified or possibly did not identify units in positions that were visible from the road, because, as I have said before, to drive off the road in certain areas was not a wise move; therefore, our visibility of what the VJ or the MUP were doing fairly close to the road was limited in certain occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think it may be that we're talking slightly at cross-purposes because towards the end of May do you recall there having been an offensive moving from Pec?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so. I made a statement at some stage that, yes, the temper of operations increased during that period, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We will come to some of the documents in a little more detail later on today, and just to complete the picture with this document. BG-3, that is combat group 3, is then - and I'll just read the language into the record first - "is to be ready in the current redeployment sector for operations along the following axes: Pec to Decani to Rastavica to Junik to Ponosevac village; Pec to Zahac to Klina to Iglarevo village; and Pec to Rausic village, Barane village, and Celopek village." There the task is described as follows: "In cooperated action with MUP forces, break up DTG along the axes of engagement and cooperate with BG-2 to unblock Ponosevac village and the Morina border post and secure the Pec to Decani route and the Pec to Klina route." Taken together, and leaving aside the question of implementation, this appears to have been a plan then, looking at these two combat groups together, to mount a pretty substantial offensive from Pec, both in an easterly and in a southerly direction and, indeed, in a westerly direction. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That appears to be the correct -- the drift of the order, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you turn, please, to page 5 in this document and to paragraph 17. Now, you may remember that I asked you some questions on the last occasion about the likelihood that a concentration of Serb artillery, for example, in an elevated position around the lake, would be guarded by ground troops operating on the ground as a sort of cordon sanitaire, and we had some discussion about that being a normal, appropriate military tactic in the British army and in other European armies. I just wanted to ask you about this. Paragraph 17 reads in the context of this redeployment by the 125th: "Extend advance security and outguard sentinels in the redeployment sector of the units and at positions and use them to control those sectors that are difficult to observe, or from where sniper ... fire and automatic rifle fire can be opened at units or MTS. Within the scope of b/r, determine the axes of movement for personnel and MTS where personnel will be protected from surprise DTG operations from a distance." Now, pausing there for a moment, a couple of abbreviations could you help us with. Do you know what MTS indicates?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought you might be asking that. To be honest, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. And b/r?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might be, Your Honours, brigade. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. But in broad terms, is that paragraph ordering outpost ground troops to conduct protective operations in areas which are not easily visible?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would suggest that this is a standard procedure to be followed; whether it was followed, that is another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that is what's written in the order for normal safety precautions around a deployment area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And could you just explain in perhaps more straightforward language than paragraph 17 does what that standard deployment would consist of?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: So bearing in mind that the troops concerned, both the VJ and the MUP, had been operating in this area, we're talking May for nearly three, four, five months, one would expect them to have a good, if not very good, knowledge of the area, or they should have had. That depends on their patrolling ability. And, therefore, they should be able to pin-point potential areas of problems and take the appropriate actions to safeguard themselves. Now, that is presupposing that they carry out the correct military actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. All we can deduce from this document is what is being ordered?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The orders are clear to protect the lines of communication from interference.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And in practical terms, just to spell it out for the record, that would mean putting ground troops into locations in the redeployment sector where there may be concentrations of, for example, KLA who could pose a threat to the troops that were being redeployed into those areas. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect, it's not necessary to put troops in -- directly into areas. A military expression is you can cover an area by fire from an elevated position, rather than exposing troops to guerilla tactics at a disadvantage.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you'd need to be in a position to fire into the area if there was any movement?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That would be useful, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And would you expect sniper -- snipers to be used for that function?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are we talking about the Kosovo Liberation Army?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, the Serb sentinels?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would think that they would use a combination of both sniper and both direct fire from armoured personnel carriers and tanks and indirect direct fire from other artillery or mortars.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So the intention, taken together with the first part of this order, the intention underlying the instructions here set out includes the provision of fire-power to cover an area of redeployment which moves from Pec to Erecka Suka and to Lake Radoniq; in other words, move south from Pec to those two locations?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the written order, sir, and it says to break-up or destroy, I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- which indicates that a fairly heavy weight of force could possibly be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just finally this: "Advance security and outguard sentinels." What do those terms mean in military terminology?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, so they could cover a variety of -- it could be mobile forces, well protected; it could be the special forces, who, as I indicated, are better trained; it could be just heavy, ordinary forces grouped with heavy fire-power and the ability to withstand any small attack that may be mounted against them. So there is a variety of options.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Looking at paragraph 14, the instruction includes an instruction to mine the redeployment areas. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says "mines." So these could be what we called protection mines, not, you know, to physically mine it, to block it, but to mine, to protect your own defensive position. So these mines may not be left there. They may be put, deployed when you are in the area for you are own protection; and as you withdraw from that position, you then take them back with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Which is what the second part of paragraph 14 seems to imply, I think?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In order to lay mines, presumably, there would need to be ground troops for protection?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's always better if that is done, but these protection mines can be are laid by the ground troops themselves because they are laid close to them in order to give immediate protection against surprise attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you turn please to tab 15 now for a moment, because I think you indicated earlier on that obviously your ability to observe the conduct of particular offensives depended on the access that you had to an area at any given time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: May I make it clear, this is a document which should not be shown on the public screen. For the record, it currently has no MFI number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That should be assigned an MFI number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D721, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, if I can just allow you a moment to orientate yourself, Colonel Crosland, with this document. It's a situation report dated the 28th of May. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the date, time group, on it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, in essence, I'm going to suggest to you that what you're reporting here is a situation whereby you were being denied access to the area around Decane by the Serb forces whilst the end-of-May offensive was being conducted, but that you were able to see the consequences in the village of Ljubenic on the main Peje to Decane road. That is the general suggestion to you; but before you respond to that, perhaps we might look at some of the detail. First of all, in the summary, at the bottom of page 1, I'll just read it into the record: "Two-day tour of western Kosovo; freedom of movement more restricted than normal (could not get to Djakovica and Decani); Village of Kijevo (south-east of Klina) in hands of armed Serb civilians; saw evidence of recent house burning in two villages north of Decani - witnesses tell of helicopter attack on two small villages to the west of Rudnik; witnessed the arrival of large MUP convoy in region; also saw large JSO convoy returning towards what we believe is its base location; No evidence of VJ involvement in actions. MUP turning the screw." Now, I want to look at that in a little more detail, please. First of all, if we turn over the page, paragraph 2, under the heading: "Restriction of movement," and allowing yourself a moment just to read that paragraph. Do you have that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Taking it shortly, does it appear, therefore, that your party was being denied access to the Decani area, first of all, by Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, as written, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And does it appear that because of the way in which the check-points were each of them turning you back, that there must have been a central order to keep internationals, that is diplomats and the press, away.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That appears to be correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that coincided with a significant increase, did it, in MUP forces in the area?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As stated on my report, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you did, I think, manage to get as far south on the main road as Ljubenic and Gornji Streoc because we can see in paragraph 4 that you made a visit to those two villages. So if I can just pick it up at paragraph 4 under the heading of: "House burning in villages north of Decani." Unfortunately, as is often the position with your situation reports, a line gets chopped off at the bottom of the page. We often miss a line, so we have to pick that paragraph 4 up in the middle of the sentence, but it reads: "... of the buildings astride the main road in Ljubenic and Gornji Streoc had been strafed," presumably strafed with gun-fire, Colonel Crosland?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "The spent cases had not been there more than a day or so. Some of the houses were burnt out. One in Gornji Streoc was still smoldering. The MUP was not in sight." I'm just allowing the transcript to catch up. "The villages appeared deserted, but after a short while a number (20) of Albanian men came out to tell us what had happened. They said that the villages had been attacked and 11 people were killed. The attacks took place on Monday, the 25th of May. Their descriptions of the perpetrators match the JSO rather than the regular MUP." There's then for a few lines a description of one of the Albanians to whom you spoke who had a jacket with AK-47 magazines in it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One moment, please, Mr. Emmerson. You now may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, pausing there for a moment, do you remember that occasion?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to see - and I appreciate you had a great deal to follow-up on, and there was a great deal going on Kosovo-wide - but do you remember whether there was any follow-up to that, whether you conducted any other inquiries or picked up any other information from anywhere else about what had happened on the 25th of May in those two villages?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think the report is as full, as I can recall, sir, bearing in mind that the situation, as I said, was extremely fluid and changing very often, you know, from minute to minute, as one side or the other locally got the better for a short time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could I just ask you very briefly to look behind tab 39, which is a report from the OSCE covering --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, tab 39.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, if you are moving to another tab, I'd like to ask one additional question or will you return to this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm coming back to this one. I'm most definitely coming back to this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Tab 39 will need to be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that will be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be D72, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, this is a Kosovo Verification Mission summary of events in Kosovo, which cover both 1998 and 1999; and in this section, it deals with it village by village. And if you look at the second page of the selection there, you can see the village of Ljubenic referred to and the report reads as follows: "Ljubenic just off the main road to Decani, seven kilometres south of Pec, is a mixed village situated at the foot of steep cliffs rising high above the plain. It was the site of a reported mass killing on the 25th of May, 1998, in which eight people were extra-judicially executed by the Serbian police." And there is then a footnote which I'll come back to in a moment. "At that time, independent verifiers were unable to reach this area of heavy fighting. During fighting which began a few days later, about 40 houses were destroyed or severely damaged and most of the Kosovo Albanian population moved out." And the rest deals with 1999. Now, the footnote is set out on the following page and is footnoted to an Amnesty International report, and then immediately after that is an extract from a web site called the Kosovo Crisis Centre which has a number of photographs with the rubric: "Lybeniq, 25th of May, 1998, attributed to Koha Ditore." Now, pausing for a moment there, would you agree that the OSCE report appears to be referring to the same incident that you came across the aftermath of; in other words, Lybeniq on the 25th of May, 1998?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That appears to be in the same area, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So although they were under the impression that independent verifiers had been unable to reach the area at the time, you had, in fact, got there at least within the three days of that attack?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That appears to be correct, sir, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Koha Ditore, I think you said - I may be wrong about this - but did you not say Koha Ditore was what you regarded as a reliable Albanian source?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the major source within Pristina, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it appears as though, without commenting on the detail of the photographs, it appears as though the account you were given of a number of people - I think you were told 11, is that correct, having been killed by the JSO - is supported at least by other reports of that incident. Would you agree?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That appears correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the photographs, if they are indeed victims of that attack, are all individuals in civilian clothes?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: They appear to be in civilian clothes, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we can move a little further down.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did Your Honour have any questions on tab 15 on the passage I had already dealt with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I had. I would like to draw the attention of you, Mr. Crosland, to the second paragraph where it reads in the middle: "Decani has had the largest MP presence in the last month." I wondered what "MP" here stood for.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, which page are you on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm on tab 15, second page, paragraph 2: "Restriction of movement," approximately in the middle: "Decani has had the largest MP presence in the last month."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that should read "MUP," sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I guessed to be the problem.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's a typing error.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we go back then to paragraph 4 where you've had this conversation with the villagers of Gornji Streoc and you'd also visited Lybeniq. Just a little lower down from that, you say this: "We left after a short while and proceeded to a MUP check-point just north of Decani. The MUP, after consulting with their superior HQ by land-line, refused our request to go to Decani. Whilst waiting at the check-point," somebody, whose name is redacted, "asked about a shot-up VW Golf. The MUP said that on Monday, the 25th of May, two MUP were travelling from Pec to Decani when they were ambushed in one of the villages to the north of the check-point. One was killed and the other wounded. It is plausible that the actions against the two" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You go on to observe: "It is plausible that the actions against the two villages," that is Lybeniq and Gornji Streoc, "could have been sparked off by this ambush. The VW had Montenegrin number plates. We returned to Pec." Now, Colonel Crosland, I just want to ask you one or two questions about that passage because you seem to be of the view that those attacks on those two villages on the 25th of May, the same day as the shooting or ambush of this Golf containing MUP members, that those attacks might have been retributive attacks. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said many times, this key axis, the major route from Pec down to Decani on to Djakovica and Prizren, was fought over on a daily basis; and, therefore, opportunity targets to both sides, both to the KLA and the MUP/VJ, were engaged as and when these were offered. Therefore, I think it is quite plausible, as I've said, that this was a retaliatory -- possibly a retaliatory attack, having lost two MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, what I want --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it could have been part, as you are indicating, of a larger operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I just want to look at that in just a little more detail with you. You're clear that you were told that one of the two MUP in the Golf had died. Is that right? That's what you've recorded at least?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I recorded, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We've heard evidence in this court from a witness who was a member of the MUP who was driving in a Golf motor car from Pec to Decani on the 25th of May with another MUP officer and a civilian and whose vehicle was opened fire on by a group of young KLA soldiers or volunteers and the vehicle was damaged. And the witness who gave evidence here was struck in the leg and injured, but nobody was killed in the incident. And what I'm trying to explore is the possibility that the two may well be one and the same. We know that the incident that the witness who gave evidence here described was said to have taken place on the main road that day near Lybeniq. Do you remember whether you were told that the attack that's referred to here on a Golf motor car was an attack that had occurred somewhere in the vicinity of Lybeniq?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, all I can do is repeat that what is written in my report is as accurate as I can make it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But the Golf when you saw it, at least, three days after this incident was located, was it, at a check-point north of Decani, so it seems in any event?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, that's what's written in the report. That's where it was, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But I suppose it's far too long ago for you to remember whether that check-point was near Lybeniq or closer to Decani?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. I mean, as I've tried to indicate to the Court, there were -- there were many check-points, I believe strong points all the way up and down that road which were put in position as and when instances arose. So I'm afraid I cannot be any more specific than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I entirely understand. But just returning then to the comment you made a few moments ago. One possible explanation for the attacks and killing of civilians in those two villages is retaliation; another is that they were part of a wider offensive radiating south from Pec. And is it fair to say that you're not in a position categorically to say which of those two is the more likely explanation?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I entirely agree, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we look briefly at paragraph 8 for a moment, please. It reads: "JSO convoy moving east out of Pec en route for base 2. As we were entering Pec last night, we saw a JSO convoy, ten vehicles travelling east towards" it says, "Vitromirica. The vehicles were all painted in their unique camouflage. Some had JSO badges on their vehicle doors. This is unusual. All the JSO wore camouflage paint." Is that paint on their faces?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "They were in good spirits. Some Serbs waved to them. They shouted back in a triumphal manner. This afternoon we found what we believe is their base, a prison to the east of Istok. A BOV-3 in their markings was parked in a hangar (5 BOV-3 was in their convoy last night). We believe another JSO location is the hotel above and to the west of Decani monastery." Paragraph 9: "No evidence of VJ involvement. No one we spoke to mentioned VJ involvement. Once questioned they spoke of JSO, PJP, or MUP involvement." And then two sentences further on: "We believe that the VJ is giving materiel support, vehicles repainted blue, logistics, et cetera." Pausing there, the BOV-3 that you saw in the possession of the JSO is one of those anti-aircraft weapons that was being deployed for anti-personnel use; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was. That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, again, this is obviously one of those occasions when you've recorded your belief that vehicles of the VJ were being repainted blue. Can you just be clear for us, the JSO vehicles that you describe, would they be blue?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. As they are as described in their unique camouflage patterns.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. So when the VJ vehicles are being - if I can put it this way - re-allocated, it is re-allocated to the MUP and the PJP?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I understand, they would be re-allocated to the MUP and they -- internally, they would then decide where they would deploy them.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then finally this, under paragraph 10: "MUP turning the screw." Can you just explain for the record what you mean by that expression.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I've said to the Court before, the major axes across -- or the major routes, rather, across Kosovo had been blocked for some time, for some weeks. And it appeared now that the Serbian security forces, as a whole, were starting a more comprehensive policy to attempt to try and clear the area and to -- also to maintain some authority over the major communication routes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think on one previous occasion when describing that expression, you indicated, in effect, that what was being utilised was a policy of general wanton destruction and dislocation of normal life for the Albanian population with the aim of making the place uninhabitable. Is that a fair summary?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a correct summary, sir, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But as we can see under paragraph 10, would you agree, the information that you were able to obtain about how this offensive was, in fact, being conducted was information that by and large you could only pick up from speaking to individuals who had been in the area rather than observing it for yourself?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect, sir, I don't think that's entirely true.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: We, as I indicated, were in the area for a considerable amount of the time on a continuous basis, and the assessment was based on my professional ability, but, of course, we were not privy to the direct orders that were issued to the Serbian security forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we turn now, please, to tab 16. This is again a document that does not have an MFI number yet. It is on the 65 ter list. It is a draft translation; and, therefore, if there is a perfected translation, we will ensure that it is substituted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D73, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Colonel Crosland, this is a handwritten in its original --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, Mr. Emmerson. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: In its original form, this is a handwritten document, ordering certain deployments. It's headed: "PrK," that is Pristina Corps command, dated the 28th of May, and addressed to the PrK command and the 3rd Army to the commander or the Chief of Staff. And, in summary, it describes military action that was being planned and taken as part of what I suggest at least is the end-of-May Serb offensive. Can I ask you to turn to page 3 for a moment. "I have decided" at paragraph 3. "I have decided: "In coordinated action with MUP forces, unblock the Sisman-Ponosevac-Molic-Junik route and the Ponosevac-Donja Morina-Potok Molic route. Group the main forces to unblock the road along the axis of Ponosevac-Molic-Junik and group auxiliary forces along the axis of Ponosevac-Donja Morina-Potok Molic." Again, pausing there, those are all villages on the western side of the main road and consistent with the order that we looked at a little while ago. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That appears to be correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Two lines further down: "Be at the ready for engagement by 0400 hours on," and then there's some uncertainty about the date, given the date of the document is the 28th of May, it says: "2/? 8 May 1998. "BG-2 of the 125th Motorised Brigade, together with the 30/2 PAT/30-millimetre, double-barrelled anti-aircraft gun/platoon from the 52nd arbr PVO/anti-aircraft artillery rocket brigade, in cooperated action with the MUP forces are to unblock the Ponosevac-Molic-Junik and Ponosevac-Donja Morina-Potok Molic routes. "BG-2 of the 549th Motorised Brigade is to unblock the Sisman-Smonica-Popovac route. "BG-3 of the 125th Motorised Brigade is to unblock the Pec-Rausic-Ljubenic route. The 3rd bVP is to perform in-depth security of the state border and a diversionary advance along the axis of G. Pavle Ilic border post-Decani-Crnobreg." Continuing: "The 52nd bVP is to launch a diversionary attack along the axis of Radonjic Lake to Donji Bites village, while the 52nd arbr is to launch a diversionary attack along the axis of Djakovica-Cabrat-Osek Hilja." And over the page: "Have a tank platoon, a bVP plant and a 30/2 PAT platoon on reserve," and then various weapons are referred to. If we can look at the bottom of that page: "Situation in the territory. "Check-points and Serbia MUP patrols are operating according to plan: "The territory controlled by Siptar terrorists stands as in the previous days. It was noted that terrorists in Glodjane village are undertaking comprehensive preparations to fortify the village." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's written there, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, looking back, please, at the two aspects of the manoeuvres at the bottom of page 3. The 3rd bVP is to perform in-depth security of the state border and a diversionary advance along the axis of the G. Pavle Ilic border post-Decani-Carrabreg, and the 52nd bVP a diversionary attack along an axis from Lake Radonjic to Donji Bites. Now, Donji Bites is adjacent to Suka Bitesh, is it not? It's a village close to the lake?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember, sir, if you say so. I don't recall the village. It's not on the map that I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, we can clarify the position as the day progresses. But do you have the map with the red circles marked upon it available to you? If not, we can just provide you with a copy of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's D32 that the witness is being shown now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, before you proceed, you said that the document under tab 16 was in the original handwritten; whereas, I see that there is some handwriting as far as the date is concerned; but the document, as such, doesn't seem to be handwritten.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I had taken that from the typed script which says: "Handwritten" at the top.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Handwritten must be the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it says 28.05.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it makes complete sense in context because on the type script, it says: "Handwritten 28th: May."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can the witness be provided with this map which is rather easier to see than the one he's marked. This is D32, and it's the map that we're all familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to orientate yourself, do you see the lake and Radonjicka Suka, the hill immediately to the west of the lake at 571 metres above sea level?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And immediately to the west of that are a smattering of houses along a road there, do you see that, against D. Bites?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that is, obviously, one axis of diversionary advance from the lake towards Donji Bites, whilst there is taking place at the same time, or planned to take place at the same time, a diversionary advance from Decane to Carrabreg, which we can see immediately south-west of Decane. Now, first of all, those two advances are, in effect, a pincer movement towards Gllogjan, are they not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what they appear to be, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: At the end of May. What exactly is a diversionary attack?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a diversionary attack is supposed to hide the main thrust of another operation that may be being planned or be in concert with the diversionary attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So to draw the attention of the enemy into an area where you can engage them and - if I may put it this way - approach them unaware from a different direction?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could be one way of putting it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that would imply, would it not, that what was being planned here was a --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just one moment. Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That would imply, would it not, that what's being planned here is a diversionary attack up to Donji Bites village in order to draw KLA attention in that direction and away from Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is possible, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it would appear, at least from the last two lines in this document, would you agree, that special attention was being paid to the preparations that may be being made in Gllogjan village for this attack?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's, again, what is written down, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we turn then, please, to tab 17. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is D34.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I can take this very briefly. This is an order of the same day signed by Major-General Pavkovic; and just casting an eye over it, can I ask you to confirm that this is an order apparently directing a military offensive on the western side of the road, the western side of the main road, from Decane towards Locane, Slup, Voksa, Junik, and from Varic and the Erenik stream; in other words, look at the document as a whole and the places there referred to it seems to be ordering a simultaneous attack to take place on the 28th of May on the western side of the road. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So looking at those orders together, and looking at the evidence of what you found in Gornji Streoc and Lybeniq and the fact that despite the troop build-up in the area, the internationals were being excluded at this point in time, do you think on reflection what was taking place was a major Serbian offensive on both sides of the road?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what the orders have been issued to carry out, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And I think, if we turn -- MR. EMMERSON I'm not sure that that last document was marked for identification, was it? It was. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we turn behind tab 18 now, not to be shown to the public, which is a DipTel, you can help us with this, which may be describing the aftermath once you were able to get some more information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson. Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we move to tab 18, you suggested in your question to the witness that D34, as you said, seems to be ordering a simultaneous attack to take place on the 28th of May. The witness confirmed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I see at this document is that it bears the date of the 28th of May, 1998, that from what I understand - but let me check in the original - that it is supposed to bear a stamp at least, that's what the translation says, which I have difficulties to find in the original as it appears on my screen. Yes. I might have the wrong one in front of me. I searched for D34, but could you give me the Defence number. Would that be 1D04-0008?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not tiff. Now, I have it in the is it system as a one-page document so I can't look at it; but in the translation, it says that it was received at the 28th of May, and then unclear, at 20 minutes past 8.00 at night.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And in the first full paragraph at the end --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- it reads: "On stand-by the 29th of May, at 4.00 in the morning."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So I wonder what made you suggest that it was planned as an attack on the 28th of May and what made the witness confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think it -- I'd have to check the precise words that I used, but what I was intending to say this was a 28th of May order for activity to take place in the early hours of the morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think we looked at this document once before and I'm sorry if I used shorthand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And I'm still wondering where the second page in the e-court is.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We will need to check that. It is possibly a stamp on the rear of the single page, but we will need to check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It could be. That should be copied and then reproduced in the e-court system as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If I can go back to tab 18 not to be shown to the public, and I think not yet ascribed an MFI number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then Madam Registrar, for tab 19 --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Tab 18.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, tab 18 bears P99.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. So it's P99 that I'm looking at, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is a report for the 4th of June. "There are reports" under "Security." The heading, "Security," under paragraph 2. "There are reports that fighting continues, mainly in the Decani area of western Kosovo. My DA has reported that he was turned back... north of Pec and south of Djakovica, so we have no independent information." Pausing there. This is presumably Ambassador Donnelly reporting back to London some of the difficulties you had experienced getting into there?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Then paragraph 3: "There are also suggestions that the security forces are expanding the area of their operations. Some reports speak of shelling and police movements near Glodjane and Jablanica, KLA headquarter cases east of Decani; security force sources claim that 1.000 KLA supporters are based in Glodjane." Now, pausing there for a moment. Do you recall there being reports of police movements near Gllogjan at that end-of-May/beginning-of-June period?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think as we indicated, sir, there are movements all along this major axis.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. But Gllogjan is some distance to the west of the main road and there may be some significance in police movements as well as shelling in the heartland area of Gllogjan.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it would be true to make an assertion, sir, that the VJ or the Serbian security forces had indications where there may have been possible KLA bases and, therefore, they may well have shelled these potential positions --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- as they had shown throughout -- sorry -- I beg your pardon, sir. As they had shown throughout the context or the contact in Kosovo, which I think I've tried to indicate on many occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I mean, shelling I think we've heard a fair deal about. But the report here is speaking not merely of shelling of Gllogjan, but of police movements near Gllogjan. Now, presumably police movements means police movements across the ground?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. With respect to you, Mr. Emmerson, this is Ambassador Donnelly's report.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: He has taken my previous -- or the previous report that I made and he is now adding to it from other intelligence sources --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- that I would not be privy to because I was on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just bear with us for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. Yes. I had understood that when Ambassador Donnelly reported to the foreign office, he was doing so not merely from your own information but from other intelligence available --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- but presumably he wouldn't have reported police movements near Gllogjan unless he had some information regarded as reliable that that's what was taking place?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are other intelligence sources, overhead sources, that could possibly have confirmed that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Exactly so --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- which again I wouldn't be privy to being out on -- I mean, it's part of normal procedure that if someone is out on the ground gaining information, then he's not necessarily told the information in order that the information can be verified are not --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Independently?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- independently, and if you can get access to the area. And on this occasion, as I have stated in reports, access was denied, quite understandably, when military operations were underway.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But just for the sake of clarity, the language used by Ambassador Donnelly there, where he distinguishes between shelling on the one hand and police movements near Gllogjan on the other, that expression "police movements," accurate or not, is a report to London that there are police movements on the ground near Gllogjan, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it is stating.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say, it may well have come from other sources that I can't verify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, I'm looking at the clock if you can find a suitable moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I will. It may be just now, in fact. Would Your Honour just give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just finally this, Colonel Crosland. In a statement that you made in July of 2004, commenting on this document, you said that it generally referred to fighting around Decani that you recalled as "a raging battle." Is that a fair description of what the information was that you were picking up; in other words, that there had been a major offensive and that there had been military activity, including military activity in the area of Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. It comes from a statement of mine based, as I have indicated to the Court, on a lot of reports that were sent back, both verbally and by secure phone. I think it would be fair to say that there was a huge amount of military activity in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would that be a convenient moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That would be a convenient moment, but let me just make two observations. First of all, I don't remember the history of tendering P99. I noticed that there is no translation in the e-court system in a language the accused understands; but since I see that you're cross-examining on it without making any reference to the absence of such a translation, I take it that this is accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That is accepted. Would Your Honour just give me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think, just in answer to Your Honour's question about the provenance of it becoming P99, subject to correction from Madam Registrar, we believe that to have been one of the documents that yesterday morning was ascribed a number, although -- I can't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would be surprised if it bears P99 because we are far beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. We may need to check this, because it is undoubtedly a Prosecution document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. I'm not that much interested in the history as such, but I just noticed that it is not available in a language in which exhibits usually have to be available.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So far as my client is concerned, that is not a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is not a problem. If that would be different for other counsel, then I would like to hear. Then, finally, the last line on the first page disappears on the copy. If there would be a better copy, that's both true for the hard copy and the electronic version, if there would be a better one to be uploaded, that, of course, would be preferable.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As I indicated earlier on, this is a systemic problem with the sitreps and the DipTels. There is very often a line missing at the bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll adjourn and have a break until 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we turn, please, to tab 19, Colonel Crosland.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is a document that requires marking for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D74, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For the record, it is a Pristina Corps command order assigned by commander Major-General Pavkovic, and it is dated the 10th of June and there is only one passage I want to turn to, it is on page 2, under the heading 3: "Situation of the corps units."

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The corps in this context would presumably refer to the 3rd Army as a whole. Is that correct, Colonel Crosland, the Pristina Corps of the 3rd Army?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, within the 3rd Army as the major formation, the 52 Pristina Corps is presumably the corps that General Pavkovic is referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the corps actually based in Kosovo, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And there's a passage there that begins by referring to the fact that the corps units, during the day, the 10th of June, have been executing tasks successfully, that its focal point was to secure the border and communications and various villages there set out to the west side of the main road. And then just halfway down that paragraph, there's a sentence that reads as follows: "During the day, officers of the PrK command in coordination with the IKMs have positioned the KSJ units in the following areas of deployment." Pausing there, do you know what the IKM acronym would be?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It is obviously Kosovo --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're on page 2 of 5, are we?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. If you don't know instantly, then don't worry. We'll find out from somewhere else?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It actually means forward command post. It's on the first page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mr. Re is quite right. The words -- the acronym IKM is translated on the first page as forward command post.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And KSJ is an abbreviation the translators didn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know what those letters might stand for, Colonel Crosland?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not an abbreviation I'm familiar with.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Carrying on, the positions then of various units are described. If you can find the third bullet point, there is a reference to the "72nd SPECBR," that is special brigade, "IDC/reconnaissance-sabotage company - in the area of Maja Coban." And then this: "The 25th CVP/military police company/in the area of the Radonjic Lake (subordinated to the 52nd BVP/military Police Battalion). Safe and stable communication has been established with all units." There are two formations referred there: The 25th Military Police Company in the area of Radonjic lake, which is then subordinated to the 52nd Military Police Battalion. Can you indicate for us what your reading of that paragraph is; in other words, what it's telling us.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 72nd Special Brigade are formation troops who were brought down into Kosovo and were extant of -- in the order of battle, they would be VJ headquarters troops based from Belgrade. So they are not an original part of 3rd Army and 52 Corps in the province of Kosovo. The other unit, 25 military police, appears to be a subunit of the 52nd Military Police Battalion, which would probably make sense.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Given that the rubric, before the bullet points, indicates that the units referred to have been positioned in the following areas of deployment and given that the last sentence of that sub-bullet point refers to the establishment of safe and stable communication, does this indicate some sort of reinforcement or additional troops being placed in that position, in your view?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's a reasonable assumption to make, bearing in mind that Lake Radonjic was probably a vital area of control for the Serbian -- the Serbian security forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, of course, we know that they had already been stationed there for some time because you yourself had seen them shelling from there at the end of July?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think the military police would have been shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Another unit would have been shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we turn to tab 22, please. I'm going to take these documents at a reasonable pace. Tab 22, again, is a VJ document signed by Colonel Lazarevic, the Chief of Staff, and it's dated --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It would need a number?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, it would need a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D75, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it's dated the 23rd of June. I want to go through this in just a little detail, if I may. Paragraph -- under the heading: "Very urgent to the commander," the first paragraph refers to a verbal order issued by the commander of the 3rd Army and based on current needs, and with the aim of taking the Radonjicka Suka feature." Do you know what the word "feature" means in that context, "the Radonjicka Suka feature"?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I presume it is an important ground feature of tactical significance.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: A little lower down underneath the order, there is a formation described. Can we just go through it. "The formation of temporary BG," that is combat group, "5 forces with the following composition." So this appears, would you agree, to be an order that a new combat group, a temporary combat group, with a name combat group 5 should be created with the following subcomponents. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what appears to be written there, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the components are: "Command, communication squad, and a medical squad from the 52nd arbr PVO," that is, Anti-aircraft Rocket Brigade. Then: "A 30/2-millimetre PAT/30-millimetre, double-barrel anti-aircraft gun/platoon from the 52nd arbr PVO (withdraw the platoon from the 52nd bVP/military police battalion, and in its place engage a 20/3-millimetre PAT platoon and a BOV-3/self-propelled anti-aircraft gun/from BG-1)." Can you help us in summary terms with what that is describing?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to state that the anti-aircraft assets are being re-organised within this new battle group --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And does that --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- as stated, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And does that then apply also to the following line: "120-millimetre MB/mortar/platoon from the 549th Motorised Brigade (to be withdrawn from the 52nd bVP)."

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That fact appears to be correct there, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And then: "A mechanised platoon from the M-80 bVP of the 243rd Motorised Brigade (on reserve at the IKM)," which is the forward command post. So, overall, this is a reallocation of VJ forces to create a new combat group 5 temporarily for some particular purpose.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That appears to be correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the purpose is to take some feature on the land of military significance in the area of Radonjicka Suka?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That appears to be correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And just at the bottom there, we can see two infantry squads. Do you see that --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- as a component of this grouping?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just so we're clear, what would be the approximate size of two infantry squads, and what is the significance of them being described as infantry squads?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: A squad could be, in American terminology, anything between eight and 15 to 20 men. So, we in the British army, we refer to sections and platoons. A squad is, I think I'm right in saying, in American language would be about eight to 15 to 20 men.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. So the fact that they're described as infantry squads, does that tell us anything as to what their deployment or function would be in this operation?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suspect they're there for protection of some of these static assets.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As ground troops, in effect?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So when we discussed earlier on whether you would expect there to be ground troops operating on the ground to establish a cordon sanitaire around artillery positions, does this assist you in answering that question?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: They could be used for that particular task, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: A little bit further down, the deployment of BG-5, number 2. "Deploy BG-5 to the Donji Bites village sector in Radonjicka Suka by the 4.00 o'clock on the 23rd of June, 1998." Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's written there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: "In coordinated action with the 52nd bVP and making use of Radonjicka Suka, prevent operations by DTS/sabotage and terrorist forces/along the axes of Rznic village to Glodjane-Donji Bites-Gornji Ratis-Donji Ratis-Rakoc, and Gramocelj-Donji Bites village." So there is a series of axes there described, included Rznic to Glodjane and Ratis, in which there is clearly a determination to--

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, may I ask you to slow down --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- especially when you are reading these lists of many names.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Would you agree, Colonel Crosland, what is being described there as the function of BG-5 is to prevent KLA from operating along the axes that are there described?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those are the written orders written given--

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- to the troops. Whether they were carried out or whether they were prevented, of course, is a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. But that is clearly the intention of this deployment?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That appears that is in the orders of the paragraph, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Of course, all of those axes that are there described are right in the heart of the area you marked on your map and around the canal, are they not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are indeed, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And how would the BG-5, including their ground squads, how would they go about preventing KLA free movement in those areas?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, with respect, you would have to ask that question to the VJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean, I think if I understand what you're getting at, sir, as I've said all the way along, there is more than sufficient Serbian forces to carry out this particular operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
