utterances.text: What is it, if I may respectfully suggest, is that question is their ability to carry out this type of military operation, and that's where we have a difficulty or possibly a difficulty, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But in terms of stated intention, if you were to try to carry that stated intention into effect, you would need, would you not, either to have paramilitary anti-terrorist police operating on the ground, or at the very least snipers able to take shots at KLA operatives as perceived moving along the axes that are described?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: With respect, sir, that is one way of doing it. There are many ways of doing an encircling movement. There is what I would call the very heavy -- the very heavy option of using ordinary troops or perhaps a more precise operation of encircling with the use of aircraft and helicopters rather than what I would call a direct assault, which was more likely the norm of the Serbian forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to follow that question and answer up a little bit. If you want to cut-off, let us say, a group of KLA insurgents based in Gllogjan using the tactic that you've just described, the expression you used, I think, was encircling. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So you would need to ensure that there was no obvious avenue of retreat. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be, yes. It would give you more chance of success.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. In catching and eliminating?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what is required, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you know from the geography that you had a focus of attention on a KLA headquarters in Gllogjan here, but also that there was a KLA headquarters in Jablanica, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, sir, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So militarily, if you're encircling Gllogjan, you've got to cut-off the retreat to Jablanica, have you not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you want to try and achieve a proper objective, then, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: But if you are prepared to let people disappear for various reasons, which would be too long to go into here, then you can leave them an avenue down which to go which may be mutually beneficial for both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But that would be an intentional strategy to drive them to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you were trying to encircle them you would have to cut off the route, wouldn't you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be wise to do that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And the direct route from Gllogjan to Jablanica would take you across the canal area, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could do so, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So if you were trying to cut-off that avenue of retreat, you would need to have some ability to control that area, would you not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as I've indicated, if that's what you wanted to achieve.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, may I draw your attention to the fact that I think on the last ten or 15 questions you put to the witness that the answers were usually introduced by: "If this," "if that," and, of course, I mean, if you want to achieve certain thing, it might be wise or you could use -- I mean, that is of limited -- in limited terms assisting the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand. Can I just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't want to stop you immediately but let's avoid --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I understand Your Honour's point. In one sense, one could say that about any order from the VJ because it's only a statement of intention, which needs to be interpreted and applied in context, and one doesn't know to what extent it was carried into effect. But in understanding other evidence in the case, knowing that that was the military strategy that the VJ was seeking to deploy and what its implications would be may, in our submission, be of assistance to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nevertheless, I would like to draw your attention to the fact that it struck the Chamber that so many "ifs" are in play at this moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Finally on this document, paragraph 3 describes the route to be taken towards Donji Bites village, and it indicates it is to start at just after 1.30 in the afternoon on the 23rd of June. And paragraph 4 indicates that "taking over of Radonjicka Suka feature and a section of the features in Donji Bites village is to be to the done by the Djakovica SUP." Do you see that over the page, point 4?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So this, again, is clearly a joint VJ/MUP operation that is being planned here?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And this was a time when you were being told in all communications with the VJ that no such operations were taking place. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was being denied at the time, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can we go to tab 23 now, please, and this should be a document not shown to the public and it needs an MFI number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, tab 23 would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D76, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, and under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think everything's that's not shown to the public should even, if only marked for identification, be under seal. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This, Colonel Crosland, is a 13th of July sitrep. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the date on the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I just want to ask you about one or two passages, please. Over on the second page, page 2, just halfway between the punch-holes, there is a line that says: "Tour 10 July 1998" and a route is set out for the tour, which I won't read out for the record. It then says, "Comment CLN. "UCK Rudnik area. About 30 UCK seen including German and Dutch personnel, 2 times RPG 7 and spare bombs located at initial VCP otherwise only rifles, pistols, and grenades. UCK admitted no COMMS between groups." What does that last sentence mean: "UCK in Rudnik admitted no COMMSs between groups"?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think on this particular occasion when I asked did they have radio communication between their groups, that was the answer I was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And "their groups" being?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The groups here around Rudnik, which is quite a long way from Pec --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- on the northern route towards Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I pick it up then, please, at the bottom of page 2. "Pec-heavy MUP/JSO roulement took place during PM. Approx 150 fresh-faced and heavily armed JSO drove south through Pec to probable holding area around Decane. More JSO seen driving repeatedly around Pec and others openly drinking close to BKS. All MUP positions also received fresh personnel with clean uniforms and bergens, new faces see at VCPS. 20 assorted vehicle convoy passed tour at Prilep VCP going north, final vehicle fired two bursts of automatic fire into Prilep area." And then paragraph 5: "Wanton damage. Each successive visit to Decane/Pec area highlights continuing damage being inflicted by MUP/JSO forces randomly shooting up homes/houses/businesses and pilfering contents. VJ also involved in further damage to Crnoljevo." And then finally at the bottom --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Then, finally, at the bottom under the heading, "Abnormal force," there is a reference to the use of heavy weapons primarily against human targets. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just one or two supplementary questions, please. This is obviously a report of which you are the author. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's, in fact, signed by David Landsman.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. Would you have had an input into this?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that particular time, yes. The reason I'm hesitating because I was back in the UK in --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For your daughter's wedding I think.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, sir. I was back here, yes. I would agree with all the analysis here, which I think is fairly evident from all my other reports. So none of that there is sadly anything out of the normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What is clear, though, is that there's been a fresh influx of forces into the JSO. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And when it says, "openly drinking close to barracks," was that a phenomenon that you were generally aware of?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I think we were surprised to see, bearing in mind that there were not many vehicles on the road apart from ourselves, that they were openly advertising a rather lax attitude to discipline.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Drinking, meaning drinking alcohol and getting drunk. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, I mean, drinking and military operations, in my humble opinion, shouldn't go together.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Tab 24 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson. I'd like to ask one question you were earlier asked about the 10th of July tour. There it reads, and I just don't understand, that "about 30 UCK seen, including German and Dutch personnel." Suddenly foreigners appear, which is unclear to me. Could you explain?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour, I will try. During the course of 1998 when I was touring around all of Kosovo, we deliberately made it our business to try and get to know and find out what the UCK or the KLA, the Kosovo Liberation Army, was all about. On various occasions, when we were apprehended by the KLA, it was quite clear that there were foreigners within their ranks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Being mercenaries or?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes. And I had -- sorry. I had other intelligence that indicated that foreigners were coming or were spreading from the ongoing situation in Bosnia into Kosovo itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for this explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just to pick up there. When Judge Orie asked you whether they were mercenaries, are you implying that there were people who were being paid money to fight with the KLA or that they were people who were not Kosovo Albanians who were volunteering?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason I'm hesitating, sir, is I can't remember specifically whether we had intelligence as to whether they were mercenary troops, i.e., being paid to fight, or whether they were just mercenaries who were looking for another job to tide them over until yet another troubled area erupted. So I can't specifically say they were being paid as mercenaries; but as we are all well aware, there are people who travel around the world going from trouble spot to trouble spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Can I turn now to tab 24, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is another document signed by Colonel Lazarevic, Chief of Staff. It's dated the 15th of July, 1998, and it needs a marked for identification number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D77, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it's just to maintain the picture of consistency. If we look at point 7, the following report is being sent to the commands of various battalions: "From today on and for the next seven days, the KLA is planning to attack the VJ in the Radonjic Lake sector, as the VJ's deployment there is preventing them from achieving their aims." You see that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Tab 25, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This needs to be admitted under seal, not shown to the public, and given a marked for identification number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D78, marked for identification, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Again, I think this is a situation report dated the 30th of July. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the date on the document, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, in the summary, there's a description of various matters which are the content of the report, including the attack that you had witnessed from the Lake Radonjic area to various villages, which we discussed when you last came to give evidence. And I think we looked at this document very briefly then in order to fix the date of that four-hour shelling operation that you witnessed. I just want to look at one or two other aspects of it quickly. The last sentence of the summary records, does it, the concern that was mounting in your mind and that you were seeking to communicate to the foreign office; namely: "How do Serb authorities explain wanton damage to towns and villages." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Generally speaking, as I said, we looked at this document before. It describes, amongst other things, the four-hour shelling incident that you witnessed. Is it right, Colonel Crosland, that you raised this with General Ojdanic?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is one of the instances that I raised with him, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, again, is it right that you told him what you'd seen; namely, four hours of direct and indirect fire on Junik, Prilep, Rznic, and Glodjane, and told him that thought it had created a demonstrating security and humanitarian situation? Do you remember telling him that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I remember those phrases, sir, or similar to that was used, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And did he agree with you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember, to be honest, sir, and I may have stated that in one of my reports; if so, as I said before, I have no intention of misleading the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You can't honestly remember now.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've made so many statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. You don't remember what his reaction was when you put this proposition to him, that this was disproportionate force?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think and hoped that there'd been a growing awareness that the continues massive damage being inflicted by security force operations would eventually have to be called to order; and, therefore, one was trying to warn them of the future dangers of this particular tactic. It didn't seem to be taken onboard, as is evident, during the latter part of 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Can we look briefly at page 3. There are various subparagraphs there, Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, and so forth. The first Bravo refers to: "Wanton damage. Every village adjacent to both avenues into Malisevo having suffered damage. Houses and businesses burning and garages deliberately vandalized," and so forth, "crops and vineyards burnt, some animals killed." That's something you witnessed yourself?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct; and as it says in Charlie, the troika group of ambassadors were shown this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I drop now to the next entry that says Charlie because I think we start again at 7 Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, so just opposite the second hole-punch. You witnessed, it seems, eight low-loaders carrying bulldozers and earth-movers, travelling towards Pristina. Did you come to understand what function bulldozers and earth-movers had in the VJ military operations in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think in many terms they were used to dig fairly instantaneously fortifications for guns, artillery, not necessarily for, you know, totally destructive means of bulldozing houses. So it was used as a defensive mechanism, I mean, obviously they could be used in other ways as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Did you ever see machinery of that kind being used in Prilep to destroy the houses?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that, sir, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. Can we go then, please, to tab 26.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This again needs to be admitted under seal, not shown to the public, and given an MFI number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D79, marked for identification and under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I want to take this, if I may, fairly briefly. This is a situation report dated the 7th of August. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the date on the document, sir, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you refer in the summary to: "Ongoing operations on Drenica, Junik, and possibly Jablanica areas in villages north or south of the Peje-Pristina road and the Gornji Klina-Rudnik-Rakos road wantonly destroyed and there being increasing damage to infrastructure." And other similar entries of the sort that we've seen in other documents. I just want to be clear. This is the 7th of August. Were you aware in the period around this time Serb troops were building up to take Gllogjan?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, as I've indicated, sir, that it was fairly obvious that some kind of major operation was probably being put together to carry out various objectives.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We've seen in this courtroom - and if it's appropriate during the next break I might ask you to watch it, but I don't want to take up time in court sitting times - a BBC broadcast of a piece of news footage of a journalist in Gllogjan and Irzniq on the 11th and 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It is, for the record, Exhibit D69.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It shows paramilitary police having taken control of the area and moving in. I just want to know whether you now recall there having been a major sweep of Serbian paramilitary forces into that area in the first few days of August; in other words, around about the 11th or 12th of August.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I think I've tried to indicate, sir, the operations were ongoing on both sides throughout the summer or the early spring, summer, and autumn of 1998. I mean, to tie me down to a specific period, I mean, the answer is no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I meant do you specifically recall in the first half of August there being an occasion when Serb paramilitary troops overran the KLA completely in Gllogjan and Irzniq and forced them out?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that at the moment, sir. I may have made a report to that effect. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm not trying to test your memory.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: We can't find references to that in your report, even though there is, I think, no dispute that it occurred ?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, if I may, forgive me for interrupting. As I said, I think some reports were redacted and others were taken out by the Ministry of Defence or whoever, Your Honours; and, obviously, I'm not aware of this procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So it's possible that there is a report dealing with that but that it --

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. There may well be gaps in the reports which I can't answer that question, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I will ask in the next break if you could take five minutes of the time to take a look at a piece of footage that we've all seen in court to see if it refreshes your memory in any way, but I won't take any time on that now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The practicalities of that, Mr. Emmerson, need some setting up, as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I've set that up already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then, Mr. Re, I take it that there's no objection against D69 being viewed by the witness outside of court?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, of course not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Tab 27, if I may, please. This looks really at the other side of what was going on as this military operation was being planned and put into effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is a document which does not need to be under seal and can be shown, and it needs to be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D80, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is a plan. Would you call this an OrdBat or not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I think it is just an handwritten commander's intent signed by General Pavkovic, that this is what he is attempting to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I see. So it's a general overview of the military objectives.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: For the sake of the record it's dated the 1st of August, 1998?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it refers to a meeting of the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija held on the 31st of July, 1998, in Pristina at which it was decided to "launch the third stage of the plan on the 2nd of August, 1998." Now, first of all, were you then aware, that is to say, were you at the time aware of the existence of the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, as I've said to the Court before, sir, it would have been unusual if there had not been a Joint Command. They had not -- or the authorities, excuse me, would not admit to a Joint Command.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know what is being referred to where Colonel Pavkovic refers to the third stage of the plan?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not. I'm obviously not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well, very well. And then if we look at the details it was decided: "1. To crush the terrorist forces' centres in Likovac-Ovcarevo villages and Jablanica and Glodjane villages and Smonica village by mounting synchronised operations in the Drenica and Jablanica areas and continuing the blockade of Junik and Jasic villages." It instructs, "bring units to the OR," that is the waiting area, "on the 1st of August and start operations early in the morning of the 2nd of August." And then 2, a reference to exerting psychological pressure on terrorist forces in Junik by continuing the blockade. You see those entries, Colonel Crosland?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I do, sir, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, perhaps I'm unduly focusing on what's handwritten and not.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Crosland, you said earlier that this is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Command --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- handwritten. Here, again, I think the only thing that is handwritten is the date, and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. It's the same pattern as we saw before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know how whether an operation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: By the way, Mr. Emmerson, I have to correct myself. Where I said it's the date, it's the number rather than the date because the date is even typewritten. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you know now whether at the beginning of August the operation that you say was being planned to put into operation, do you know whether steps were being taken at the beginning of August?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only way I can answer that, partially, sir, is that in the reports that were issued at the time, I think indicated a building of pressure by the Serbian security forces to do something about the unstable situation across KiM, Kosovo-Metohija, and the three areas mentioned are arguably the three key areas within this area of operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As I said to you a moment ago, there's no dispute, I think, and there's certainly video film footage which you'll see, that by the 11th of August Serb forces were closing in and had overrun Irzniq and Gllogjan. The issue that I'm seeking to explore with you through these documents is the process running up to that; in other words, the putting into effect of that operation in the week or two beforehand. Could we, to that end, please, look behind tab 28 just for a moment, which is a report from Commander Cirkovic referring to the plan that we've just been looking at apparently. It's dated the 7th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this would be Exhibit Number D81, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I just want to look at paragraph 1 with you, please, on that report. It's a report of the 7th of August to the Pristina Corps command. "Between the 25th of July and the 6th of August, MUP units were engaged by decision of the Joint Command for KiM along the following axes," and then various axes are set out, including at the bottom the axis from Gllogjan village to Jablanica village. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, of course, we discussed that earlier on, but the axis of Gllogjan village to Jablanica village would take you across the area where the canal flows, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it appears, does it not, from this paragraph that by the 6th of August, Serb MUP troops had already conducted operations along that axis?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to these documents, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes, assuming their authenticity. This is not a statement of intent, but a statement of what had already happened. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, sir. I mean, the first axis is along the major -- the main Pristina to Pec road --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and the second one, as you've stated, between Gllogjan and Jablanica, which is a lot vaguer because the two are in a cross-country area --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- which could have gone across the canal area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may not have done. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But the canal area does, does it not, flow right through the most direct route from Gllogjan to Jablanica?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That very axis?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Tab 29, please. This is a recorded decision by Commander Lieutenant-General Pavkovic dated the 10th of August.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D82, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: My general suggestion, once we've looked at it, Colonel Crosland, is that this is the final assault being planned on Gllogjan and Irzniq after the area around had been secured over a day's proceedings. So we had the position up to the 6th of August as the axes are cut off and the Serb forces close in on the ground, and this I suggest is the document which shows the final plan to move in on those two villages. So number 1, Lieutenant-General Pavkovic says that he has decided: "With MUP and VJ forces, smash the DTS stronghold and establish control over the general Crnobreg village-Rznic village-Glodjane village-Gramocelj village-Prilep village sector, using the main forces along the Donji Bites village-Savar village-Saptej village-Glodjane village axis and the Gramocelj village-Babaloc village-Rastavica village axis, and the auxiliary forces along the Crnobreg village-Beleg village-Rznic village axis and the Crnobreg village-Prilep village axis with the following aim: By attack and active operations against the flank and the rear, with diversionary operations and support from VJ combat groups, smash and push back the DTS from Gjakove-Decane-Peje road, then destroy the enemy in the general Crnobreg village-Rznic village-Glodjane village-Babaloc village-Prilep village area, and after that capture this area and prevent further operations by the DTS." Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, sir, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is an operation of encirclement, isn't it, of the kind you were describing earlier on?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That appears to be the case, yes, sir, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's a process of approaching over land over a period of days in the build-up to this, as we saw in the last document, followed by a final assault as these forces close in for all sides, is it not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what the stated aim of the general has decided, yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And if we just look at the tasks for the units there set out, can you confirm, please, for us and for the record that BG-52 is tasked to support the attack launched by the main forces of 2nd MUP detachment and the SAJ and the PJP along the Glodjane to Saptej village axis?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that tells us, does it not, that there is a written instruction being issued that the VJ should directly participate along with all three units of the paramilitary police in the area closest to Gllogjan and the axis between Gllogjan and its nearest neighbour village, Shaptej?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's the order as written.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And, similarly, we see a collaboration between the VJ, the MUP, the SAJ, and the PJP along the axis from Gramaqel to Baballoq to Rastavica, do you see that at 2.2?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And at 2.3 .1, between another VJ unit, the 1st Motorised Brigade, attacking with the main forces along the Gramaqel to Gllogjan axis and auxiliary forces along the Gramaqel to Dubrava to Shaptej axis?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Where -- in paragraph 1, it refers to main forces and auxiliary forces, having read this document now and bearing in mind the heading: "Combat disposition," which is subcategorised as attack forces, support forces, active operations forces, and blockade forces, can you just help me with one or two of those terms. What do you understand the distinction in this battle plan between the main forces and the auxiliary forces to be?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, as you've just read out to the Court, sir, the attack forces are -- units are indicated in paragraph 2; with paragraph 3 is fire support; paragraph 4 is, again, combat support measures which are laid out in detail --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- intelligence support, engineering report, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 5, logistical support and ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What are blockade forces?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would presume that they may well be forces that are put around the around the outside to try and encircle any irregular forces that may be in -- may be contained.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So, again, it confirms the view that the rest of the documents give us, that this was an encirclement operation of the kind you described earlier on. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think the geographical layout of the various axes would indicate that, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Could we turn now to tab 30, please. This is a document --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you do so, Mr. Emmerson. D82 is Rule 65 ter number 492. Under that number we find two documents which seems to be two copies of the same document. Now, we also find translations. Let me first say the one document starts with K022-8031 and continues until 8034. The other one bears the number K035-6688 and continues until 6691. Although these clearly are different versions of the same typewritten document, the one - and that is the first one I mentioned - bears some handwriting on it; whereas, the other one - that's the second I mentioned - bears a stamp on the top of the first page. Now, surprisingly, the translations are the same. One of the translations just mentions the K022 series; whereas, the other translation at the line at the bottom also mentions, apart from the K022 series, also the K035 series I just mentioned. The problem is that the translation being exactly the same as it appears at first sight make reference to a handwriting which appears only on the K022 version --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- whereas, the K022 version also contains more handwriting, which is not comprised in the translation, which is common to both documents. The Chamber would very much like, unless there's any specific reason to have the handwriting at least, should become clear - I'm also of course addressing you, Mr. Re - that there would be only one document and the one to be used.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is whether with or without handwriting, if handwriting is relevant, of course, it should be the one with handwriting; if relevant, then we could do without handwriting. And the translation should not mention any handwriting text which does not appear on the document; and if there's handwriting text on the document, it should cover all the handwriting text.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could we turn just briefly behind tab 30 now. Tab 30 is P309 and it's a document we've looked at fairly recently with another witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This is an ECMM report and ought to be not shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it shows the immediate aftermath of the operation that we have just been seeing the plans for, and you can see in the first paragraph there that under the headlines: "UCK strongholds in Glodjane and Rznic destroyed." And then under the heading, "Kosovo, main items," it says: "Team Pec reported a heavy attack launched by the Serb artillery and 80 tanks against Glodjane, Rznic, Prilep (17 kilometres south of Pec) on the 12th of August. Glodjane and Rznic have been completely destroyed." You see that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you, in fact, we know, went on the 8th of September to the canal area along with, you described the organisation as KDOM. It may be that the organisation that accompanied you was Team Pec of the ECMM, which sometimes also described itself as KDOM. Does that sound right to you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: This pattern -- I'm sorry. Did I say Team Pec? I meant, for the sake of the transcript, at line 23 of the transcript, I said, "Team Pec of the ECMM." I should have said, "Team Prizren of the ECMM." Does any of this jog your memory of this attack in the first half of August?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand, actually, what the question is leading to.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm just wondering whether looking at these materials in any refreshes your memory about that part of the Serbian offensive that took Irzniq and Gllogjan at that part of August.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I already stated that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Forgive me if I'm not understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No, it's my fault I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't quite understand where we're going because I stated on several reports that when we were taken in to visit the site, that there was heavy fighting still going on. Prilep was certainly very heavily destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I think we've talking -- I'm sorry, I think we're talking at cross-purposes. You went in on the 8th of September and saw that operation continuing, and I'm going to come to that when I ask you some questions about the canal. What this series of documents is referring to, and the film that you'll see in the break, is an operation that had taken place a full month before, in which that area had been brought under the control of the Serb paramilitary police, and I wonder whether that jogs your memory in respect of the fact that there had been such an operation a month before you went there, as well as one that was continuing while you were there on the 8th of September?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think all I can repeat, sir, is that there were ongoing operations throughout the entire time and one operation ran into the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I don't think I can be any more helpful than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. The last document, then, I wanted to ask you about in this series is behind tab 31, and it is a document dated the 18th of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That needs to be given an MFI number, and it is an 18th of August order of General Pavkovic's.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D83, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Colonel Crosland, the reason I was asking you those questions about this month interval between these two offensives taking place on the same two villages is related in part to this document. We see on the 18th of August, look over the second page on page 2. If you look at 3.9: "Withdraw the 52nd bvp/bomber regiment from Radonjicko Jezero," that is the lake, "to the Kosovski Junaci barracks and transfer the positions to MUP forces. The forces from the battalion in the old barracks in Djakovica, the strength of one company, are to be on stand-by to fight the DTS. Transfer artillery group 2 from Lake Radonjic to the Pec garrison and organise the hardware. Give the troops a break and then engage them by a separate order. "Regulate the time of when the MUP is to take the positions and the withdrawal of AG by a separate order." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And does that imply, given the knowledge that you had of the deployments in the lake, that right in the middle of August the decision is being taken to withdraw the VJ forces and to substitute them for paramilitary police?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is what is written in this particular document.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Well, that is the last in this series of documents that I wanted to ask you about, and I now want to move on to ask you some questions about your visit to the canal.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I don't know how Your Honour wants to plan the rest of the morning. It would be an entirely convenient moment from my point of view to take a break; and then as I indicated earlier on, Mr. Guy-Smith and I have discussed cross-examination and we will be sure to have concluded by quarter to 2.00 between the two of us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I do not mind whether we have a break now and then have another time to go, or to have to break later.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: From my point of view, it would be good to take the break now and move on to a fresh topic after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll have an early break and we'll resume at 25 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can I indicate to Your Honours that Mr. Guy-Smith has been kind enough to indicate to me and through me to Your Honours that he will have few, if any, questions for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Just so that Your Honour sees the use of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And we took a bit more time. We had to deliberate on a certain issue during the break. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Colonel Crosland, you had an opportunity briefly to look at the BBC film footage from the 11th and 12th of August. Can I just ask you two or three questions about it. First of all, I assume from the answers you've given already that you do not recall having seen that piece of broadcast footage at the time?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. The scenes are only too reminiscent of what I saw with my own eyes throughout the summer and autumn of 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Secondly, the Serbian ground troops that we see in that piece of footage, which are described in the voice-over as paramilitary police, are wearing two different kinds of uniform, a blue uniform often with a jacket with ammunition clips in it and a camouflage uniform, and we see a number of them with bandannas and so forth. By this stage in the summer; in other words, by August, were the various groupings sufficiently distinguishable for you to be able to tell us from that observation who it was we were looking at; in other words, which contingents it was in the village of Rznic and Gllogjan that are shown in that film?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have thought they were mainly PJP and possibly JSO.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. And finally this: We see some of the PJP or JSO officers with a yellow ribbon tied to their shoulder, and we've had a number of -- certainly one other explanation for what the significance of that yellow ribbon is. Can I ask you, please, formally to confirm for the record that the significance of the yellow ribbon is simply to prevent blue on blue fire; in other words, to prevent Serbian paramilitaries from shooting other Serbian paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's certainly to prevent or to try and eradicate blue on blue fire between forces, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, I want then to move to the 8th of September and to the occasion when you visited the canal. First of all, can I ask you this: I think it's right, isn't it, that you were first alerted to the fact that there was a site which was being described as a mass grave site by KDOM. Is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't honestly remember --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Mr. Emmerson, whether it was KDOM or whether it was the local MUP that came to us in where we were based at Djakovica at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: As I said, I've said on many occasions, I'm not in any way trying to test your memory here. Can we look behind tab 33 together, please, which is the sitrep in which you deal with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It needs to be marked for identification, admitted under seal and not shown to the public.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, that would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D84, marked for identification and under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So this is your situation report for the 10th of September, referring to, as we see just two-thirds of the way down the page, the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: -- referring to the Kosovo situation on the 8th and 9th of September, 1998, and item 1: "Potential grave-site," and I'm just reading this into the record, "two kilometres south-east of Irzniq" and then there's a grid reference. "Eight to 12 bodies seen Serbs claim 40 because 40 other people are missing. Chinese rounds found in the area which would indicate UCK responsibility. Autopsy to follow." Now, pausing there for a moment. It might be easier before I ask you any questions about that to turn to the passage in which this is dealt with in more detail, and that's paragraph 5 over the page. "Potential grave, at 081600B, September 1998, tour was called by KDOM to meet ... at Djakovica in order to be escorted to the above site. Tour was taken through Prilep and Irzniq, both villages totally gutted, 90," presumably 90 per cent, "of houses destroyed, and haystacks burning. "Heavily armed MUP/PJP/SAJ with VJ, T55, and Praga in support. MUP mortar line times 4 firing in support from Prilep. At," and then a grid reference is given, "eight to 12 bodies were observed, some badly decomposed, indicating approximately one month old, others were fresher in water canal and appearing from earth on side of canal. Fifteen splash marks seen on concrete side of drain indicating possible execution. No details of who these people were was given. Autopsy to follow. "Comment. Troops involved in this op were obviously still conducting further ops and attempting to secure the area. They looked tired and on edge." Now, just having looked at that document again, there are various questions I want to ask you about it, if I may, and about the events that it describes. First of all, I just want to come back to the description you give there, and you've dealt with it in your evidence in chief so I won't take a great deal of time over it, of what it was that you witnessed on the way in to the area. Returning to the question that I began with, first of all, does that refresh your memory as to whether it was, in fact, KDOM who first involved you or brought this to your attention?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what is written there, sir, so that is what is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Do you remember whether you were told by any Serb official how long before your visit the site had been discovered?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall any time-line, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Was it your impression that you were being brought to the scene immediately or soon after its purported discovery?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that appears to be a fair comment, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And before forensic teams had arrived; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I can't confirm, sir, because I don't know what their forensic teams would be dressed in.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were people there who appeared to be collecting evidence. Whether they were forensically trained or not, I cannot confirm or deny.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well. I don't wish to jump straight to the canal. I want to ask you again about the operation on the way in. You told us, I think, in your evidence in chief that there were some 300 or so forces, Serbian forces, combined forces, involved in the ongoing operations that you witnessed on the way in. That's 2971, line 12. That's a large number of ground troops committed to this operation. Was there any resistance taking place to the firing that you saw in Prilep and in Irzniq? Was there anyone on the other side?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no return fire coming back, as far as I'm aware.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And as well as burning and looting --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And as well as burning and looting, you described on various occasions seeing shooting into houses in Prilep. Shooting with what? Fire-arms or heavy weapons or tanks or what?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was mainly, if I remember rightly, small-arms, automatic rifles, and machine-guns, but it was quite clear that heavier weapons had been used by the splash marks and other damage that had been inflicted on these villages. But again, these villages, if I may say so, had been under assault as we've heard on several occasions. So there was a cumulative effect of damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, that's really what I wanted to come to. Prilep, you say, I think, was no more than 18 inches high. It had been flattened by then. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But when you gave evidence about this in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, if you speak slower, then we don't have to stop again and again. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: When you gave evidence in the Limaj trial about this journey in - this is transcript 1969, line 11 - you indicated, as I think you have on other occasions, that you were aware as you saw this operation in Irzniq that this was either the second or the third time that the JSO and SAJ were - to use your words - clearing the village. In other words, you knew that Irzniq had been overrun before?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That has happened, as I have indicated to the Court, across large areas of Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I understand that. But it's very important just to focus in on Irzniq for a moment because it is clear from your testimony I think today, as well as in Limaj and in some of your statements, that when you saw these operations taking place in Irzniq on the 8th of September, you knew that this was not the first time that the paramilitary police had overrun that village. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reason for that statement, sir, is that at the -- on the main road from Decani down towards Djakovica where the road from Prilep comes in, there had been an MUP check-point for the majority of the summer --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- which was attacked on many occasions from that area; and, therefore, it's not surprising that the Serbian security forces would go out and attempt to eradicate the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And launch military assaults on Irzniq, not simply Prilep, the front line, if I may put it that way, but on Irzniq, which is why I think you opted outside of the red line as a disputed area on your map. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Prilep is literally within metres of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Irzniq is --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: A little further on.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- a couple of kilometres further on. Again, within the area of operations to try and produce some kind of "safe" zone for the Serbian forces to patrol into.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But it was your understanding that they would periodically launch and overrun Irzniq over that summer period. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you know presumably that Irzniq runs immediately next to the canal -- I'm sorry, runs immediately next to and through Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: The canal does?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I remember rightly, the canal is a little bit further to the east, but from what --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think if you trace it up --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think you can see the canal on your plan, if you trace it up, it runs pretty much directly into the village of Irzniq?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was just looking at the grid reference given for the --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- possible site, which is slightly east of Rznic, but the canal goes on to the north and, therefore, close to Irzniq, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Are you able to give the Trial Chamber any sense of how many times you would have expected or understood Irzniq to have been overrun in that way?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I object to the question, "expected." On what basis can the witness possibly --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Sorry, I'll rephrase the question. It's a perfectly legitimate objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: You've given evidence that it was your understanding that the Serb forces would periodically launch and overrun Irzniq in that summer period up to the time when you went to the canal on the 8th of September. Can you give the Trial Chamber any further sense of what you would understand by the word "periodically."

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, Your Honours, it is quite clear from the operation orders that have been produced as evidence that the Serbs had massive and capable forces, well capable of mounting an operation off their main axis to cover both Prilep and Irzniq at any time they chose. It's a question of whether they wished to do so. And as I said, the situation became a tit-for-tat operation where security forces would be shot at and killed on the main road, and then the security forces would counter-attack in a variety of ways. That could be a more complicated and detailed operation or I suspect the local commander could decide to take the initiative into his own hand and attempt to follow-up terrorist activity by doing what we call a clearing operation, which is literally a, as I stated, a clearing operation. It does not necessarily mean that they hold the ground for any length of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. But they would periodically gather a force and enter in as far as Irzniq in order to clear the area of KLA concentration and push back the threat to the main road?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that's what you're reading from one of my statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I'm summarizing.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: But you would agree with that proposition?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think, when you drove through Prilep and Irzniq, you were in your red Land Rover Defender with a very big Union Jack clearly identifying this convoy as a convoy of international diplomatic vehicles. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's as far as my memory recalls, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Does it surprise you that these operations continued despite that fact there was an international presence entering the area?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I made that statement in one of my previous statements, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And it surprised you because what you were witnessing was grossly disproportionate force, is that right, and you were surprised that would be happening under the eyes and under the nose of international diplomatic representatives?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think "surprise" was no longer a word one used. It was unfortunately an all-too-regular occurrence, whether we witnessed it or not. And one can understand the vehemence and the anger of security forces when they lose people, as I have lost people to terrorist action. That doesn't mean to say one in any way will condone what I've said many times. It was extremely heavy-handed action, but again we have to deal with the type of troops concerned and, as I say, the very vehement strife between the Kosovo Albanian and the Serbian security forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Can I put it this way and ask you to comment on this. Was your surprise, as you put it earlier on, that this carried on despite the presence of a diplomatic convoy driving through, does that reflect a sense that really it was shocking that troops would be -- feel comfortable to conduct that sort of operation before the eyes of international observers?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think -- Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Is that what you were trying to convey?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the point one was making was that despite, I hope, a fair and accurate report on what the situation in general was, both Serbian security forces and Kosovo Liberation Army, that people were still openly flaunting -- you would hardly call it the Geneva Convention because it was far from it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I move on, please, to the canal itself and back to your situation report. First of all, we can see in paragraph 5 and in the last line of the first block of text that you were not given any information on the identity of any of the individuals whose remains had been seen in the canal area. You weren't given any identification information. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. All the Serbs I think indicated that -- I think these were Serbian personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I think as I have said on many occasions, that could not be -- I could not confirm that --

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- because I am not a qualified coroner, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And they hadn't been identified, had they, or recovered at the time you got there?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The bodies, as I indicated, sir, were still in the water or where they lay.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And nothing had been done, or you were certainly not shown or told of anything that had been done, to remove, gather, or identify any of those remains before your visit on the 8th of September?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no formal identification of the bodies by name or by nationality.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: They were just bodies at that stage?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were just bodies in the concrete canal area.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you, I think, were staying at Hotel Pashtrik at the time, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, later on in time, a makeshift mortuary was put in the basement of Hotel Pashtrik, but there certainly wasn't a makeshift mortuary there when you were there on the 8th, was there?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: None of the Serbian authorities pointed your attention to a mortuary in the basement of the Hotel Pashtrik?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. If we look at paragraph 1, that is the summary. Despite the fact that you were only being shown eight to 12 bodies, you note that the Serbs were claiming that there were 40 because 40 other people were missing. Is that how you recall it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what is written there, sir, and these reports were dictated into a Dictaphone and then typed back when I got back to Belgrade. So they are the initial, if you like, eye-witness report and as accurate as I can, you know, recall it at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Before we go on to a little more detail on what you actually saw, could you just turn behind tab 38 for a moment. This is the Joint Command minutes that we looked at when you were here last.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And that document needs to be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this will be Exhibit Number D85, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Could you turn to page -- if you look at the numbers at the bottom of the page at the right-hand side, very small, page 86 of 164. Can you see that we're looking on page 86 at a session of the Joint Command for the 4th of September, 1998, at 8.00 p.m. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: So that's four days before you arrived at the canal; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If we look at the following page, page 87, under Mr. Gajo, I think you told us before that you did not know who David Gajic was. I think that's a reference to David Gajic, who we see from the minutes at page 2, is, in fact, the assistant chief of the RDB, the state security. Do you see that entry under Mr. Gajo?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do, sir, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: The RDB, the state security, I mean, that would be the branch of the Serbian security apparatus that would engage in undercover clandestine operations, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could be one of their task, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Counter-intelligence operations of a variety of different kinds, which could involve sabotage or it could involve the commission of crimes in order to attribute responsibility to others and so on. That would be located within the RDB, that kind of counter-terrorism activity.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would probably have that area of business, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: If you look at the fifth bullet point which Mr. Gajo is informing the Joint Command of on the 4th of September, "In the village." I'm quoting: "In the village of Ratis, near Decani, there is a mass graveyard (34 Serbs, three Romanies, three Albanians)." Now, Colonel Crosland, can you help us at all as to how the Joint Command could conceivably have known the numbers and ethnicities of the remains that had not been recovered until after your visit on the 8th?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I obviously can't comment, sir, because that is what is written down here in a document that I have not seen before today, and I would respectfully suggest that Mr. Gajo is the person to be questioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it's a fairly damning indictment if it is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Rather surprises you from the picture that was presented to you, I imagine?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sadly within this time-frame, one was not surprised by the various turns that events took.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Well, I wanted to ask you just a little bit more what you mean by that, because I think you have been asked in the past whether in your view - and this is a question the Prosecution asked you - whether in your view, it is possible that the Serbs could have been involved in planting bodies there in order to up the propaganda value of this find and to blame it on the KLA in order to discredit them in the eyes of the international community. Now, please, I'm not asking you to express an opinion on whether you think that is what happened here or not because, as you will see from that document, obviously you're not in possession of all the relevant information that the Trial Chamber is or will be in possession of. But when answering that question, you said to the Prosecution that you could not exclude the possibility that there could have been deliberate manipulation of the crime scene because "the Serbs were not beyond dirty tricks for propaganda purposes. They had done it before." And I just want to ask you about that sentence. What did you mean by that when you said: "The Serbs were not beyond dirty tricks for propaganda purposes. They had done it before"?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, over the period of time in Kosovo, there were many acts of violence that were permeated by both sides, and there was a continuing and ongoing propaganda war, is probably the best word of explaining it. And that is why on my statement, which you've just gone through, I said a proper and authorised autopsy must be carried out to provide the necessary evidence to substantiate the initial claim by the Serbs that this was a KLA massacre area. I think I made that clear in my statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think even, either verbally or otherwise, warned my ambassador and other people that this whole incident may not be as is being shown by the Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: That there could have been manipulation of this crime scene, that was a warning you relayed to the ambassador because of experience of Serbian activities in the past. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I said, sir, both sides were, let's put it, economical with the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Emmerson, the dirty tricks, as such, could you help us where to find it?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm going to -- may I come back to Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It's paragraph 19, but I've lost the starting point, so I will come back to that. May I make it absolutely clear, I'm not asking the witness to express a viewpoint.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: What I want to know, Colonel Crosland, when you say the Serbs had done it before, can you give us other examples of where there had been deliberate manipulation that you were thinking of, either before or after, in order to fabricate things for propaganda purposes?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, with respect to the Court, I cannot recall. There were instances, as I indicated, on both sides that the initial evidence was not what was purported to be at the scene of the crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: And, with great respect, I don't think I can go any further than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I've told you that I myself said that we need to proceed with caution before we make an allegation; and in my opinion with the operation, the Serbian operation, going on around this area, then it behooved the Serbian security forces to provide an unbiased autopsy report to substantiate their claim.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you asked to be provided with that I think yourself, did you not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I've made that statement before, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I think your essential position was that you told the Serb authorities that if they wanted to expect the international community to take this at face value, they would need to provide to the international community evidence of a "clean-gloves" forensic investigation. That was your expression I think?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that is what was written in the report, that is exactly what I was trying to say now.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: And you never received any such information?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not that I'm aware of, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: No. Can you just turn for a moment behind tab 35 for a moment -- 35A, which is Exhibit D45. It's a photograph of two bodies floating in the canal?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, did you say 35?

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: It should be tab 35, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's supposed to be D31, isn't it, Mr. Emmerson.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You're quite right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's at least what your list tells us.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: D31, and it's tab 35A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No. 35 corresponds with D31, according to your list; and 35A corresponds with D45. The first being described as photograph of floating bodies; whereas, the second is photograph of bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I apologise, because there's a slight difference on my bundle but I've resolved it now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And perhaps we could look at what the witness sees so we can verify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes. I can see from where I'm standing that the witness is looking at tab 35, which is D31.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But it could be shown on the screen as well. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
utterances.text: Now, you've seen that photograph or a photograph very similar to that before, have you not?

utterances.speaker: JOHN CROSLOND [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. EMMERSON
